neutral_facts.value: The accused persons assaulted the deceased during a conflict that arose from a previous incident where the deceased misbehaved with women at a marriage ceremony. The deceased was chased and surrounded by the accused persons near the house of one Om Prakash. The accused persons inflicted fatal injuries on the deceased with knives, resulting in his death. The prosecution case was that the deceased was chased and held by the accused persons, leading to the fatal injuries. The evidence included eyewitness accounts and medical reports indicating the cause of death was shock and haemorrhage due to multiple injuries.

quotes.text: The deceased misbehaved with the womenfolk in a marriage ceremony. As a fallout of that incident, the accused persons assaulted the deceased. The co-accused were armed with knives while the appellants-accused were not armed.

appeal_history.value: Trial court: Conviction under Section 302/34 IPC; High Court: Conviction confirmed; Supreme Court: Conviction altered to Section 304 (Part I) read with Section 34 IPC

quotes.text: The conviction of both the appellants u/s. 302 IPC with the aid of Section 34 IPC is not warranted. The ultimate assault causing death of the deceased was the culmination of an incident which had occurred earlier during a marriage ceremony...

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the deceased misbehaved with the womenfolk during a marriage ceremony, leading to an altercation where the accused persons assaulted the deceased. The co-accused were armed with knives, and the deceased was fatally injured by them.

quotes.text: The prosecution case was that the deceased misbehaved with the womenfolk in a marriage ceremony. As a fallout of that incident, the accused persons assaulted the deceased.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that there was no common intention between the appellants and the co-accused to commit murder. The appellants were unarmed and their role in the incident was to chase and hold the deceased, intending to teach him a lesson, not to kill him.

quotes.text: The role attributed to the appellants would attract the provisions of Section 304 (Part I) IPC and not Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC. The appeal as far as the appellants' conviction under Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC must, therefore, succeed...

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the common intention to commit murder must be established, and the role of the accused must be assessed based on their actual participation in the incident.

quotes.text: The ultimate assault causing death of the deceased was the culmination of an incident which had occurred earlier during a marriage ceremony...

sentencing_rationale.value: The final sentence was imposed because the court found that the appellants did not have a common intention to commit murder, and their role in the incident was less severe, warranting a conviction under Section 304 Part I IPC instead of Section 302 IPC.

quotes.text: The role attributed to them would, in our view, attract the provisions of Section 304 Part I IPC and not Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC. The appeal as far as the appellants' conviction under Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC must, therefore, succeed...

judicial_mitigating_factors.value: The court considered the context of the incident, which was a result of a previous altercation and the deceased's misbehavior, and the appellants' role in the incident was to chase and hold the deceased, not to kill him.

quotes.text: The cause of conflict arose from the conduct of the deceased in the marriage party which ultimately as a sequence of events resulted in fatal injuries on the person of the deceased.
